steps.body: Two special numerals: 0 promises NOTHING to count, and 10 uses two marks — a 1 for the full ten, a 0 for no extras.
steps.narration: Two special numerals: 0 promises NOTHING to count, and 10 uses two marks — a 1 for the full ten, a 0 for no extras.

widget.prompt: Tap the plate that shows zero cookies.

hotspots.label: plate with 4 cookies
hotspots.feedback: This plate shows 4 cookies. Zero means an empty plate with no cookies at all.

hotspots.label: plate with 2 cookies
hotspots.feedback: This plate shows 2 cookies. A plate showing zero would have nothing on it to count.

widget.missFeedback: Look at the sides and corners of each shape, then tap the one the question describes.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — a circle is round all the way, like a coin or a clock.

predict.prompt: A plate with no cookies — does it have a count?
predict.reveal: Emptiness is countable: the count is zero, and the mark 0 records it.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw write zero ten.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw write zero ten.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

options.label: An empty group
options.feedback: Correct — zero is the written name for none at all: an empty plate, an empty frame.

options.label: A very small amount
options.feedback: Small still means SOME; zero means the counting never starts.

options.label: A circle shape
options.feedback: The mark is round, but its meaning is emptiness, not geometry.

options.label: Ten
options.feedback: Ten is written 10 — a one and a zero together; zero alone names none.

widget.prompt: Put the zero-recording routine in order.

misorderFeedback.feedback: The final step cannot come first. Begin with the amount or starting point, then finish the numeral.

widget.missFeedback: Build the sequence in this order: See the empty plate, then Count no cookies, then Write 0.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — an empty group has count zero, written 0.

widget.prompt: Which place-value story matches the numeral 10?

options.label: 1 full ten and 0 extras
options.feedback: Correct — 10 is a report: one complete ten, zero ones left over.

options.label: Ten is too big for one mark
options.feedback: It is not about size — the two marks REPORT the ten-and-ones structure.

options.label: The 0 is decoration
options.feedback: Drop the 0 and the mark reads as one; the 0 holds the ones place open.

options.label: It is a mistake we keep
options.feedback: The two-mark form is the system working: place tells each digit its job.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 2. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 12.
13 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 2 hops from 10 to land on 12.

widget.missFeedback: Count 2 on from 10: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 2 more is 12 — the teen numeral writes exactly that: 1 ten, 2 ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 2 counts past ten are needed to reach 12.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 2 numbers, on 12.

widget.prompt: Eight counters are hidden under a cup. Which numeral records their count?

options.feedback: Correct — the numeral 8 is the written name for a group of exactly 8.
9 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 8.
7 promises fewer dots than the group holds; the count reaches 8.
10 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 8.
